Abyss (Doctrinal)
uh-BIS
noun
Greek abyssos (G12) — literally "without bottom," from a- (without) + byssos (depth/bottom); rendered "bottomless pit" in the KJV and "abyss" or "deep" in modern versions. The dwelling place of demonic spirits awaiting judgment, the prison of Satan during the millennium (Rev 20:1-3), and the realm from which the beast ascends (Rev 11:7; 17:8).

📖 Biblical Definition

Abyss is the bottomless pit, the dwelling place of demonic spirits awaiting their final judgment, mentioned principally in Luke 8:31 (where the demons of the Gerasene demoniac beg Christ NOT to send them into the abyss); Romans 10:7 (where Paul applies the abyss to Christ's descent — "who shall descend into the deep? that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead"); and especially Revelation. In Revelation 9:1-11 the abyss is opened by a fallen star (an angelic being) and locust-demons ascend from it, led by their king Abaddon/Apollyon (the destroyer). In Revelation 11:7 the beast ascends from the abyss to kill the two witnesses; in 17:8 the beast ascends and goes to perdition; in 20:1-3 Satan himself is bound in the abyss for a thousand years, then released briefly, then cast forever into the lake of fire. The abyss is therefore the holding cell, the prison, the bottomless place where rebellious spirits await final disposition. It is NOT yet the lake of fire (Rev 20:14-15) — that is the ultimate judgment. The abyss is the demonic remand prison; the lake of fire is the demonic death sentence executed. The two-stage demonic eschatology matters: even the demons recognize the difference (Matt 8:29 — "art thou come hither to torment us before the time?") and beg Christ not to advance their judgment. Christ has authority over both phases — He can send them to the abyss now (as He did with the Gerasene demons, though He permitted them to enter the swine instead), and He alone holds the keys of death and hell (Rev 1:18) at the end. The abyss-doctrine is the doctrine of the universe's prison structure for rebellion: God has built it, God controls its keys, and God alone closes its mouth.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The bottomless pit; the dwelling place and prison of demonic spirits awaiting final judgment; the prison of Satan during the millennium.

ABYSS, noun. A bottomless gulf or pit; the dwelling place and prison of demonic spirits in biblical theology. Greek abyssos, literally "without bottom."

In Scripture, the dwelling-fear of demons (Luke 8:31; Matt 8:29 — "come to torment us before the time"); the realm of the dead in the resurrection theology of Romans 10:7; the source of locust-demons in Revelation 9:1-11; the prison of Satan during the millennium (Rev 20:1-3).

📖 Key Scripture

Luke 8:31 — "And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep."

Revelation 9:1-2 — "And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit. And he opened the bottomless pit; and there arose a smoke out of the pit, as the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by reason of the smoke of the pit."

Revelation 20:1-3 — "And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled."

Romans 10:7 — "Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Abyss is corrupted when it is conflated with the lake of fire (collapsing the two-stage demonic eschatology of remand-then-final-judgment), or when modernist demythologizing dismisses it as mere ancient cosmology rather than as the real prison structure of the universe.

expand to see more

Abyss / lake-of-fire conflation. Revelation distinguishes carefully: the abyss is the bottomless pit / demonic prison (Rev 9:1-2; 11:7; 17:8; 20:1-3), while the lake of fire is the final judgment of execution (Rev 19:20; 20:10, 14-15). Demons can be sent TO the abyss now (Luke 8:31); the lake of fire is reserved for the final judgment after the great white throne. Popular theology often collapses these into "hell" generically, losing the precision of the two-stage demonic eschatology Revelation gives us.

Demythologizing dismissal. Modernist scholarship often treats the abyss as ancient Near Eastern cosmology — primitive belief in a subterranean watery deep beneath the earth — to be discarded for moderns who know better. But Christ Himself treated the abyss as REAL when He encountered the Gerasene demons (Luke 8:31); they begged not to be sent there, and He honored their request (sending them into the swine instead). Christ's authority over the abyss is real; the abyss is real; the universe has a prison structure for rebellion that humans cannot wish away.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek abyssos (G12) — without bottom; the demonic prison-pit awaiting final judgment.

expand to see more

Greek abyssos (G12) — bottomless pit; from a- (without) + byssos (depth, bottom)

Appears 9 times in NT; principally in Luke 8:31, Romans 10:7, and Revelation 9, 11, 17, 20

Distinct from the lake of fire (Rev 20:14-15): abyss = remand prison; lake of fire = final execution of judgment

Christ alone holds the keys (Rev 1:18); the abyss is His prison and He alone determines who enters and when

Usage

"Even the demons beg not to be sent to the abyss before the time — they know the prison's reality and dread it."

"Satan will be bound in the abyss for a thousand years (Rev 20:1-3) — released briefly, then cast forever into the lake of fire."

"The abyss is not the final judgment; it is the holding cell. The lake of fire comes after the great white throne."
